summary: @or-sdk/idw preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`, which auto-runs on `npm install`. setup.mjs is obfuscator.io-style minified code (mangled `_0xNNNNNN` identifiers, per-call string-lookup tables) that downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<ver>/...zip` into a temp directory, chmods it executable (0o755), and then invokes it via `execFileSync` against a bundled 727 KB sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is itself heavily obfuscated (WV8StW string-array rotator plus a multi-thousand-entry mixed numeric/string constant array indicative of control-flow flattening). The README advertises @or-sdk/idw as a TypeScript client for an IDW REST API and makes no mention of a native component, Bun runtime dependency, math initializer, or install-time build step; the main entry `dist/cjs/index.js` is a plain export barrel with no top-level side effects. The Bun-executed payload is unrelated to the advertised library surface and only fires at install. Executing an obfuscated payload via a freshly-downloaded alternate runtime that is not the ecosystem's default interpreter is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern and evades Node-based supply-chain scanners; the sibling payload is not pinned by hash and its contents are opaque to Node tooling.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
